---
title: "IKEA Names and Swedish Places"
format: html
---

## Question

What kinds of Swedish places share names with IKEA sofas and armchairs?

## Data

The data come from the [TidyTuesday IKEA sofas and Swedish places project](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-10-27). The table contains Swedish locations from OpenStreetMap that match IKEA product names.

```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

ikea_places <- read_csv("ikea_places.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
place_counts <- ikea_places %>%
  count(place_type, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 8)

ggplot(place_counts, aes(x = n, y = reorder(place_type, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Most IKEA place-name matches are small settlements",
    subtitle = "The eight most common place types in the Swedish location data",
    x = "Number of matching places",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "TidyTuesday 2026-10-27 | Source: OpenStreetMap"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

Many IKEA product names match small places such as hamlets and villages. This fits IKEA's naming system: sofas and armchairs are named after places in Sweden, not only large cities.
